context.project: Food delivery platform — back service: NestJS + TypeScript, ESLint (Airbnb preset), Prettier, strict mode. Front service: React + TypeScript + Vitest.

evals.title: Can edit: add a new Programming Practice
evals.prompt: The team confirmed a new practice: every database transaction must use a transaction manager wrapper — never call raw BEGIN/COMMIT. Add it to code-standards.md.
expectations: New ### transaction (or similar) block added under Programming Practices
rule: use transaction manager wrapper, never raw BEGIN/COMMIT
why and applies to are filled
Existing practices (error handling, logging, validation) are not modified

evals.title: Can edit: add a Hard Rule from user
evals.prompt: The user says: 'NEVER run eslint --fix or prettier --write on existing files — only check, never auto-fix. Also NEVER edit .env or commit secrets.'
expectations: Two bullets added to Hard Rules section
NEVER auto-fix existing files (eslint --fix / prettier --write)
NEVER edit .env or commit secrets
Each bullet has the reason (why)
These come from the user — not invented by scanning

evals.title: Can edit: update Tools & Automation
evals.prompt: The project added Biome as a replacement for ESLint + Prettier. Update Tools & Automation. The check command is 'biome check .'.
expectations: ESLint and Prettier rows replaced or updated to reflect Biome
New row: tool Biome, enforces Programming Practices + Formatting, command 'biome check .'
tsc row (if present) is unchanged — Biome doesn't replace type checking

evals.title: Can edit: add Style Guide for a new language
evals.prompt: The project added a Python service that follows PEP 8, enforced by Ruff. Add it to Style Guides.
expectations: New row in Style Guides: language Python, style guide PEP 8, reference includes Ruff or PEP 8 URL
Existing rows (TypeScript / Airbnb) are not modified

evals.title: Cannot edit: add test conventions or test-file naming
evals.prompt: I want to add a rule in code-standards.md that test files must be named *.spec.ts and placed beside their source files.
expectations: Does NOT add test-file naming to code-standards.md
Test file naming and placement is a test convention → belongs in testing-guide.md
code-standards.md covers how to write production code, not how to name test files

evals.title: Cannot edit: add actual API field names or shapes
evals.prompt: I want to add a naming convention row that says 'POST /orders request uses fields: restaurant_id, menu_item_ids, quantities'. Add it to Naming Conventions.
expectations: Does NOT add actual field names to code-standards.md
Naming Conventions holds the CASING RULE (e.g. inbound = snake_case) — not specific field names
Actual request/response field names and shapes belong in gateway-contract.md
A row like 'inbound API field: snake_case' is fine — listing specific fields is not

evals.title: Cannot edit: add build/run commands
evals.prompt: I want to add 'npm run build' and 'npm run start:dev' to the Tools & Automation table so developers know how to build the project.
expectations: Does NOT add build/run commands to Tools & Automation
Tools & Automation holds STANDARDS-CHECK commands only (lint, format, type-check)
General build/run/test commands belong in tech-stack.md
Distinguishes: 'npm run lint' → belongs here, 'npm run build' → tech-stack.md

evals.title: Cannot edit: promote a pattern from a workflow stage directly
evals.prompt: During execute-tdd (Stage 4), the engineer notices every integration test repeats the same DB connection pattern. It wants to promote this directly into Programming Practices.
expectations: Does NOT add the pattern to Programming Practices directly from a workflow stage
code-standards.md is read-only to every workflow stage
New or conflicting convention goes to self-report first
Promotion into Programming Practices happens only via self-learn review, after user confirms
